bead.title: Implement commit_transition (vectorized atomic commit) for postgres
bead.description:
PROBLEM
CommitTransitionPort::commit_transition is not implemented on postgres (empty impl inherits Unavailable).

PROPOSED FIX
Implement commit_transition on the in-scope postgres backend(s) (pqueue-ab2e0b21): per entry, atomically (single postgres transaction) validate the claim ref (lease token + lease expiry + item_version fence), write the entry's side_records, push its lifecycle_items as ordinary claimable work, advance/validate its instance_fence if present, and finalize the consumed claim -- returning per-entry Committed/Rejected outcomes. Support request_id-scoped retained replay/conflict idempotency over the whole commit body, matching sqlite-relational's semantics (crates/pqueue-sqlite/tests/relational_commit.rs: relational_commit_request_id_replays_without_double_write).

IN-SCOPE FILES
- crates/pqueue-postgres/src/relational.rs (and/or lib.rs per scope decision)

OUT-OF-SCOPE
- RecoveryReadPort (next bead).
- commit_capabilities() advertisement (final bead, once this and RecoveryReadPort are proven).
bead.acceptance:
1. The shared pqueue-conformance commit-transition scenario (pqueue-c42136f3 / wired in pqueue-d2f0b763) passes its POSITIVE path against the in-scope postgres backend, env-gated on PQUEUE_PG_TEST_URL.
2. A live-DB test proves: bad token/bad version rejects without writing anything; request-id replay does not double-write; a concurrent claim/commit race resolves via per-entry Conflict, not a whole-body failure.
3. `cargo fmt --check` and `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets --all-features -- -D warnings` pass.
